entries.title: Speakers see one upload card per slot, and the slot's rules are enforced
entries.summary: With **Use upload slots** on, a speaker's **Files** tab shows a card for each file the session owes — name, instructions, due date, accepted types, how many files it takes — with its own drop zone. The wrong file type is refused, a closed slot says when it closed (an extended deadline reopens it), and a full slot takes revisions only. Admins see the session's files grouped by slot, with **Move to slot** in the file menu, and can always upload whatever the deadline.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Files → Use upload slots

where.path: Speaker portal → session → Files; Event → session → Files tab

entries.use_case: A medical meeting asks poster presenters for a PDF poster by one date and podium speakers for a 16:9 deck by another; each speaker sees only what they owe, cannot drop a Word file into the poster slot, and the organizer no longer sorts files by hand.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable centrally. Events created before October 2026 keep the single file request until the customer turns Use upload slots on; new and cloned events have it on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer collecting more than one kind of file per session, anyone running a Poster Gallery, or a complaint that speakers upload the wrong file or type.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific meetings (posters + decks), Informa shows with handouts, any event with per-format deadlines.
internal.gotchas: Deadlines hold speakers only — admins and API clients can always upload. A file type the slot does not list is refused even when the event-wide list allows it. Slot filters use session fields, so a session with no Format set may owe nothing; check Slot coverage. The portal shows slot cards only after the API and UI are both deployed. Public API: session-files create/upload accept content_slot_id and the content-slots list takes ?session_id= (reference update in lennd/sessionboard-public-api-docs#51).
internal.talk_track: Tell us which files you want from which sessions, and by when. Each speaker sees exactly that and nothing else — and you see who still owes what.

entries.title: Slot coverage: who still owes each file, reminders per slot, Files columns and slot downloads
entries.summary: **Program → Submissions → Files** gains a **Slot coverage** view — a card per slot with uploaded, missing and overdue counts, filters by status, format, track and date, **Export CSV**, and a **Download files** button scoped to the slot. Each slot now has its own **Reminders** (days before the due date; 7 and 1 by default) plus one overdue notice, sent only to speakers who still owe the file. The sessions grid offers **Files: *slot*** and **Files: *slot* (count)** columns, reports get `content_slots.<slot>.status`, and the Download Files wizard can take one slot and group the zip **By upload slot**.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Files → Use upload slots

where.path: Program → Submissions → Files → Slot coverage; Program → Submissions → Sessions → Columns; Program → Settings → Files → slot → Reminders

entries.use_case: Two weeks out, the program manager opens Slot coverage, selects the Presentation card, filters to Overdue, exports the CSV for the AV team and emails the stragglers from the grid filtered on Files: Presentation is Overdue — without a spreadsheet.

cs_action.note: Reminders are on by default (7 and 1 days before) for every slot with a due date on events using upload slots. Review the offsets with customers who already run their own reminder campaigns so speakers are not emailed twice.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Deadline-chasing conversations, AV handoff planning, and any customer exporting file status to a spreadsheet.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone on upload slots; especially multi-track medical meetings and shows with hundreds of sessions.
internal.gotchas: Coverage counts only the sessions a slot applies to (its session filters). Report fields `content_slots.<slot>.*` count every session, filters or not. Reminders go only to participants with portal access whose role the slot allows, once per offset, and the overdue notice once. Slugs used in reports come from the slot name at creation and do not change on rename.
internal.talk_track: One screen answers 'who still owes the deck?' — per slot, filterable, exportable, and the reminders go out on their own.

entries.title: Put a content gallery on a website you already run
entries.summary: A published gallery now has a paste-ready snippet — **search, filters, cards and playback** — that sits on your own page the way an agenda embed does. Email-gated items unlock in the widget; members-only and SSO galleries send the visitor to the gallery Site to sign in. There is no row under **CMS → Embeds**.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries; then publish the gallery

where.path: The gallery's public Site slug; paste the snippet on any page

entries.use_case: A society already owns its marketing site and wants the Session Catalog searchable there, without rebuilding the page in Sessionboard or sending members off-site for every click.

cs_action.note: Snippet 404s until the embeds deploy (lennd/sessionboard-embeds#105) and the API CORS change is live (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4384). Do not put it on the same page as an agenda/speaker embed — they share the <sessionboard-embed> tag.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asking to put the catalog or on-demand library on a site they already run; anyone comparing us to an LMS catalog widget.
internal.who_should_get_it: Session Catalog and On-Demand Hub customers with an existing marketing site; mobile-app partners who will use /feed separately.
internal.gotchas: EU uses embeds-prod-eu. The widget is the Explore view only — Hub, My list and Site chrome stay on the gallery URL. Per-surface embargo (different withhold rules for embed vs Site vs mobile) is deferred. Mobile apps should use GET /org-portal/:slug/public/gallery/feed, not this widget.

entries.title: Poster galleries collect from an upload slot
entries.summary: A gallery's **Content** tab has an **Upload slot** select: the gallery shows whatever speakers upload or build into that slot, new galleries pick your Poster slot automatically, and **Posters by file type (legacy)** keeps older events working. Coverage counts only the sessions the slot applies to. A built poster and an uploaded poster are never both current — the newest one wins everywhere.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → request Poster Gallery; then Program → Settings → Files → Use upload slots

where.path: Marketing → Poster galleries → gallery → Content → Upload slot

entries.use_case: An event with a Poster slot filtered to Format is Poster gets a gallery that lists exactly the poster sessions, shows which still lack a file, and never counts the keynote as a missing poster.

cs_action.note: Galleries created before this keep the legacy by-file-type behaviour until someone picks a slot; nothing changes for them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Poster Gallery onboarding and any 'my gallery says X sessions are missing posters' question.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Poster Gallery customer.
internal.gotchas: The select appears only when the event uses upload slots. A slot of kind Poster is what galleries and the Poster Builder look for, whatever it is named. Publishing from the builder files the PDF in the session's poster slot and supersedes an uploaded poster (and vice versa) — the earlier file stays in version history. The speaker-facing 'Build your poster' link is wired in the portal but stays hidden until the author-facing builder ships.
internal.talk_track: Point the gallery at your Poster slot and it stays in step with what speakers actually upload.

entries.title: Public API contacts fire the Contact created automation
entries.summary: A contact created through the Public API now starts **Contact created** automations, under **Created through: From an integration**. Adding a contact you already have to the event doesn't fire it. The builder also stops showing **Re-enroll** for Contact created and New Submission, which always run once per record.

where.path: Event → Automations → People → When card → Contact created

entries.use_case: Customers who load speakers or contacts through the Public API (their own integration or middleware) can now send a welcome or data-processing (GDPR) notice automatically; before, those contacts were silently skipped.

cs_action.note: Any customer with a Contact created automation who also creates contacts through the Public API: those contacts now get the automation. If they don't want that, untick From an integration under Created through.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why API-created contacts didn't get their welcome or GDPR email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Public API to create contacts together with People automations.
internal.gotchas: Only newly created contacts fire it; a POST with an email that already exists links the contact to the event without firing. It does not backfill contacts created before the fix.

entries.title: Email campaigns show the real next send
entries.summary: The campaign list and the campaign's **Upcoming send** no longer show an old date left over from a finished send. Recurring campaigns keep sending after their second run, and re-scheduling a campaign while its last send is finishing keeps the new schedule.

where.path: Event → Send → Campaigns → list and campaign detail

entries.use_case: Organizers can trust the next-send date on a campaign again, and recurring reminders no longer stop silently after two sends.

cs_action.note: Customers who reported a recurring campaign that stopped after two sends, or a re-scheduled campaign that never went out: check the campaign and re-schedule it once; it now keeps running.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A campaign shows a past date as its next send; a recurring reminder stopped; a re-scheduled campaign stayed Sent.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using scheduled or recurring email campaigns.
internal.gotchas: Recurring campaigns that already stopped before the fix are not restarted automatically; re-schedule them.

entries.title: Advocacy templates always show a thumbnail
entries.summary: Share-card templates created through Quick Launch now save a preview image, so Portal Home and the Templates page show the card instead of the **Share asset** placeholder. Existing templates without one get a preview too.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Templates; the speaker's Portal Home

entries.use_case: Speakers see the actual share card on Portal Home before they open it, which makes them more likely to share.

cs_action.note: Existing templates are filled in by a one-off backfill after deploy; nothing for the customer to do.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why Portal Home shows a generic Share asset tile.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy customers.
internal.gotchas: Per-advocate text shows sample values (e.g. Jane Smith) in the template preview until each advocate's own preview is generated.

entries.title: Copy email campaigns from another event, and clone them with the event
entries.summary: **Copy from event** on the Email Campaigns list copies campaigns from any other event in your organization as **Drafts** — subject, body, audience, theme and recipient filters re-pointed at this event, with nothing from the send. The Clone Event sidebar gets an **Email Campaigns** option that does the same for every campaign. Anything that had no match here (a role, a field filter, a theme) is dropped and listed so you check recipients before scheduling.

where.path: Event → Send → Campaigns → Copy from event; Organization → Events → Clone Event → Email Campaigns

entries.use_case: A recurring conference reuses last year's speaker reminders, sponsor updates and welcome emails in minutes instead of rebuilding each one, and the audience filters follow the new event's roles and tracks automatically.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable. Customers with Clone Events should know the new Email Campaigns clone option is off by default — tick it when cloning a recurring event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Kick-off for a recurring event, any clone request, or a customer asking to 'copy last year's emails'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer running an annual or multi-event programme on Email Campaigns; Informa and association accounts first.
internal.gotchas: Copies are always Drafts with no schedule. Automations are not copied (they live under Automations). A campaign tied to one session loses that session scope. Filters on a role, track or custom field that does not exist in the destination are removed and flagged on the done screen — check Recipients before scheduling. A clone into a different organization drops hand-picked recipients.
internal.talk_track: Copy the campaigns, open each draft, check Recipients, set the schedule. Same content, same audience logic, this year's event.

entries.title: Roles can be limited in which statuses a session may be moved from
entries.summary: On a role's **Statuses** tab, each allowed status gets a **From any status** picker. Tick the statuses the session must currently be in — for example **Accepted** only from **Pending** — so a role can queue decisions without reopening a session you have already **Declined**. Status pickers only offer the move when it is allowed, and imports, bulk updates and the public API refuse it with a message naming the condition.

enable.path: Event Team → Permissions → custom role → Statuses → Limit which statuses this role can set → From any status picker

where.path: Event Team → Permissions → Role → Statuses; session status pickers for people in that role

entries.use_case: An admin can enforce the review workflow: track chairs and marketing can move sessions forward but cannot override a final decision, which keeps Declined sessions declined without a second review pass.

cs_action.note: Existing status limits are unchanged; a condition exists only once the admin ticks statuses in the picker.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a role 'un-declining' sessions, or asks for a stricter review workflow for track chairs or marketing roles.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with custom roles and a multi-step review (medical and scientific societies, large CFPs).
internal.gotchas: Conditions apply to custom roles only — default roles are read-only on this tab, so duplicate one first. They apply when changing an existing session; a new session can always start as Pending. Admin User and organization Admins are never limited.

entries.title: Title slides attach to their sessions by default and export in a Title slides folder
entries.summary: **Attach to each session** is now on by default when you generate slides, so each session's deck lands on the session as soon as the run finishes. When you download session files, every title slide sits in its own **Title slides** folder next to the speaker's uploads — in the Download Files zip and in download bundles.

where.path: Marketing → Slides → Generate → Attach to each session; Program → Sessions → Download Files

entries.use_case: Production gets every room's opener in one folder of the export, and the organizer no longer re-uploads each slide to its session after generating.

cs_action.note: Customers who want a download-only run switch Attach to each session off in the wizard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer using Slides for show-day production, or an AV team asking where the title slides are in the export.
internal.who_should_get_it: Slides users with an AV or production partner.
internal.gotchas: Only the current title slide is exported; superseded versions stay in the file's history.

entries.title: Shrink to fit shows everyone up to 18 participants
entries.summary: With **Shrink to fit** as the overflow rule, a title slide now shows every participant up to 18 on up to three rows, whatever the maximum-participants setting. Before, an eleventh panelist was silently left off. The designer says so next to the setting and in the panel summary.

where.path: Marketing → Slides → template designer → Participants → When more people than fit

entries.use_case: Large panels and author lists render completely with Shrink to fit, so nobody is missing from the slide on stage.

cs_action.note: Templates already on Shrink to fit pick this up on the next generation; regenerate out-of-date slides for sessions with more than 10 participants.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a participant missing from a generated slide on a big panel.
internal.who_should_get_it: NAB and other Slides customers with large panels or author lists.
internal.gotchas: Past 18 a +N more chip appears. Show '+N more' still honours the maximum you set.

entries.title: Campaigns render the matched submission, and recipient.portal_login_link works
entries.summary: A speaker with an accepted and a pending submission who matches an 'accepted only' campaign now sees the accepted session in the preview, the test send and the real send — not the first one found. `{{recipient.portal_login_link}}` renders a working link instead of blank, and the advanced Sessions filter **Status** is relabelled **Submission status** to match the quick filter.

where.path: Event → Send → Campaigns → Recipients and Preview

entries.use_case: Merge tags in a per-session reminder always describe the session the campaign filter matched, so speakers with several submissions get the right details.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a speaker email showing the wrong session, or a blank portal login link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose speakers submit more than one abstract.
internal.gotchas: Bundled (one email per session) campaigns already used the bundled session and are unchanged.

entries.title: A resumed CFP draft is sent to the step with blank required fields
entries.summary: Resuming a draft used to open on Session Info, and a blank required field under **Your Information** only surfaced as an error at Submit. Submit now checks every step in order and takes the submitter to the first one that is incomplete, with the blanks highlighted, and the Review step shows a Your Information card with an incomplete status and an edit link.

where.path: Portal → Call for Presentations → Resume draft → Review & submit

entries.use_case: Submitters no longer get a dead-end error at the last step; they are shown exactly which field to fill in.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A submitter reports 'Submit does nothing' or a generic error on a resumed draft.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every CFP customer.

entries.title: A second builder tab can no longer overwrite your Site draft or undo a publish
entries.summary: When a Site is open in two tabs, the older tab now stops autosaving the moment the other one saves or publishes, shows **Changed in another tab — Reload**, and disables Publish until you reload. Before, the older tab's next keystroke silently replaced the draft and could revert a Site you had just published. Four-digit colours such as `#FFFF` are also normalised, so the logged-in portal hero no longer turns yellow.

where.path: Site → Builder; Site → Settings → colours

entries.use_case: Two people (or one person with two tabs) can work on a Site without one quietly losing the other's changes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a published Site reverting, or edits disappearing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sites customers with more than one editor.
internal.gotchas: The stale tab must be reloaded; its unsaved edits since the other tab's save are not merged.

entries.title: Blocks inside a Columns block can be edited again
entries.summary: Selecting a Text or Image placed inside a Columns block — from the inspector or by clicking it on the canvas — now opens that block's editor instead of selecting the Columns block and collapsing it.

where.path: Site → Builder → Columns block

entries.use_case: Multi-column layouts can be edited in place like any other block.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says they cannot edit content inside columns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sites customers using Columns.

entries.title: Locked dropdown fields can no longer be cleared in the portal
entries.summary: A multi-select field marked **Locked** in Manage Portal Fields used to keep a remove button on each selected value, so a portal user could empty it and watch the value snap back on save. Locked values now have no remove control.

where.path: Portal → session or profile → locked multi-select fields

entries.use_case: Locked means locked: speakers cannot remove tags or tracks your team set.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports speakers 'removing' locked values.
internal.who_should_get_it: Portal customers using locked fields.

entries.title: Session & Speaker interest forms show date-time, time, currency and URL fields
entries.summary: Interest forms built from an application only rendered number and date fields; Starts At, Ends At, Capacity and any time, currency or URL field were missing for the submitter even though the admin's field list showed them. They render now, with the same inputs as the submission form.

where.path: Portal → interest / application form

entries.use_case: Every field the admin adds to an interest form is actually asked of the submitter.

cs_action.note: Customers with an interest form that included these field types collected no answers for them until now; mention it if they noticed gaps.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why a field on their interest form never gets answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Applications customers.

entries.title: A merged contact shows once on the event team list
entries.summary: Merging two contacts that each had a portal login left both logins on the Team list, so the person appeared twice. The list now shows one row per contact, and new merges keep the login whose email matches the contact (the other is retired, restorable from Trash).

where.path: Event Team → Team; Contacts → Merge duplicates

entries.use_case: Team lists and seat counts reflect people, not logins.

cs_action.note: Portal users whose contact was deleted, or whose links were all revoked, are no longer listed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a duplicate on Team after a merge.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who merge contacts regularly (CROI and other medical societies).
internal.gotchas: Existing duplicates created before this change are collapsed in the list but their logins are not retired automatically.

entries.title: Session filters match speakers on subsessions
entries.summary: A config set or role filter on **[Session] Languages**, tracks, tags, level or format now matches a speaker whose only session is a subsession: subsessions inherit those values from their parent when they set none, and V2 role assignments count.

where.path: Event Team → roles with a session filter; config sets

entries.use_case: Track chairs scoped by language or track see the speakers on subsessions too.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A scoped role cannot see a subsession speaker.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using subsessions with scoped roles.
internal.gotchas: Draft or deleted parents contribute nothing.

entries.title: Deleting a field says whether it affects one event or all
entries.summary: The delete confirmation names the field and says whether it is an event field (only this event) or an organization field (removed from every event that uses it), with a scoped confirm button, instead of warning about every event each time.

where.path: Settings → Fields → delete

entries.use_case: Admins can delete an event-only field without fearing an organization-wide change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer hesitates to delete a field.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone.

entries.title: Campaign final preview scrolls to the end; delivery history counts read clearly
entries.summary: The Preview step's email frame no longer stops partway down the page. The automations delivery history banner now says, for example, *4 of those records (9 emails) came from 7 automations that have since been deleted*, so records and emails are not confused.

where.path: Event → Send → Campaigns → Preview; Automations → Delivery history

entries.use_case: Organizers can read the whole email before scheduling, and the delivery history numbers add up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer cannot scroll a campaign preview or questions the delivery history count.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone.

entries.title: Favicon uploads are checked for real images; remove buttons are labelled
entries.summary: A text file renamed `.png` is now rejected before upload instead of being served as the favicon. The remove (X) buttons on branding images, Team Lead links in your own messages, and Evaluations 2.0 labels were tidied for screen readers, dark mode and consistent sentence case.

where.path: Site → Settings → Branding; Team Lead; Evaluations

entries.use_case: Branding settings are safer to upload to and usable with a screen reader.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Accessibility reviews; a broken favicon.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone.

entries.title: Session reviews need this event's program site, not the org awards site
entries.summary: Evaluation Plan 2.0 session reviews only load on **this event's Program Site**. Invite emails, preview-as-evaluator, and **Open review workspace** no longer send people to the organization awards Site. If the event has no program site, the plan shows a banner and invite/notify is held until you set one up under **Program → Site**. Evaluators who still land on the org Site see that they are on the wrong site, not that they have no assignments.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → plan; Program → Site

entries.use_case: A customer who already has an awards Site invites session evaluators and they see No evaluations found — the fix is an event program site, not another copy of the plan.

cs_action.note: If a customer reports No evaluations found for event session reviews, check Program → Site for that event before the assignment roster. APWA Snow Conference 2027 (event 6253) hit this on the awards slug american-public-works-association-awards.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Evaluator cannot see assignments; Team Lead chat about portal errors; org that runs both awards and a CFP.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone using Evaluation Plan 2.0 who also has an organization Site.
internal.gotchas: Interest Form evaluation plans still use the organization Site. v1 plans are unchanged. Creating the event site and resending from the live plan is the unblock — copying the plan is not.

entries.title: Call for reviewers: invite, import, or open interest
entries.summary: On **Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers** (Sessions 2.0), invite a named list, import last year's reviewers, or publish an interest form. Recruits pick expertise from the catalogs you turn on. Conflicts are flagged on the queue. Assignment gains **Match expertise** so people are paired with sessions that overlap those picks.

enable.path: Event → Settings → Early Access → Sessions 2.0, then Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers

where.path: Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers

entries.use_case: Societies that recruit a review committee each year can send one call — invite, import, or a public form — and assign from the expertise people actually picked, instead of emailing a list and tagging them by hand.

cs_action.note: Walk medical/scientific customers through Require approval vs auto-enroll, and confirm the event or program has a Program Site before they send invites. Interest Forms as a third host is not in this release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to recruit reviewers, reuse last year's committee, or match reviewers to track/category.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone running Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans.
internal.gotchas: Invites need an org-level Program Site (findEventProgramSite). Closing the call stops new applications; pending rows can still be approved. Import enrolls immediately; invite does not. Match expertise skips reviewers with no picks. Interest Forms are not a host in this release.

entries.title: Call for reviewers on an awards program
entries.summary: On an awards program's **Call for reviewers** tab, invite a named list, import last year's judges, or publish an interest form. Recruits pick categories and expertise. Assignment on the round gains **Match expertise** so judges are paired with nominations that overlap those picks.

enable.path: Awards → the program → Call for reviewers

where.path: Awards → program → Call for reviewers

entries.use_case: Awards programs that recruit a judging panel each year can send one call — invite, import, or a public form — and assign from the categories people actually picked.

cs_action.note: Walk customers through Require approval vs auto-enroll, and confirm the program has a Site before they send invites. Public-voting rounds hide Assign — Match expertise needs a reviewer-scoped round.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to recruit awards judges or match them to category.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone running an awards program with a review round.
internal.gotchas: Invites need a program Site. Import enrolls immediately; invite does not. Match expertise skips judges with no picks. Public-voting rounds do not show Assign.

entries.title: Email people who have not finished a portal task or form
entries.summary: On a campaign's **Recipients** step, **Portal assignment** picks a named portal task or form and **Incomplete** or **Complete**. The live count is people who have that item in that state. A recurring campaign drops people once they finish.

where.path: Send → campaign → Recipients → Portal assignment

entries.use_case: Two weeks out, remind only speakers who still owe the speaker agreement, without exporting a column and pasting emails.

cs_action.note: Ships with the Tahaluf onboarding batch. Confirm the API and UI PRs are both live before telling a customer to look for the filter.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Task reminder campaigns; Tahaluf / Informa KSA onboarding.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone chasing incomplete portal tasks or forms.
internal.gotchas: The person must already have the task or form assigned (portal membership or a direct assignment). Complete is also available if they want a thank-you send.

entries.title: Automations can fire when a date has passed or is within N days
entries.summary: People automations gain **Date field window**: a daily check on one date field. Enroll when the date has already passed, or when it is within the next N days in the event timezone. Re-enroll is available, same as a field-change trigger.

where.path: Automations → People recipe → When → Date field window

entries.use_case: Visa expiry or membership end should email the person the day it matters, even if nobody edited the field that day.

cs_action.note: Daily cron WORKFLOW_DATE_WINDOW_CRON (15 6 * * * by default). Cap 500 enrollments per scan.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Date-driven reminders that are not a field change.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical/scientific events with visa, membership or disclosure dates.
internal.gotchas: Blank dates never match. The check uses the event timezone. Sessions automations do not get this trigger.

entries.title: Task due dates can start from assignment or the request email
entries.summary: On a portal task's **Edit Settings**, **Due date relative to assignment** stamps a personal due date N days after the person is assigned, or after the assignment email is sent. Dates already set on a person are left alone. Preview and send-test do not stamp.

where.path: Program → Portals → Edit Tasks → task pencil → Due date relative to assignment

entries.use_case: A speaker added late gets 14 days from their invite, instead of sharing last month's portal-wide due date.

cs_action.note: Needs the Config_Set_Tasks due_offset migration. Changing N later does not rewrite existing Record_Assigned_Task.close_date rows.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Rolling speaker adds; Informa KSA / Tahaluf onboarding.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events that add speakers over weeks, not all at once.
internal.gotchas: A shared Due Date on the task is still the fallback. Preview/send-test never stamp. Email stamp runs only on the live assignment email.

entries.title: Hide or rename countries, and empty phones start on the event country
entries.summary: Organization **Details** has **Country list**: hide or rename countries on the system Country field for every event. Stored ISO codes stay the same. An empty phone input now starts on the event's country, from language and timezone.

where.path: Organization settings → Details; any Country or Phone field

entries.use_case: A KSA meeting can show Saudi Arabia as KSA and hide countries they never collect, while a new phone field opens on +966.

cs_action.note: Hide does not delete saved values — they stay readable. Renames are display-only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Tahaluf / GCC events; any org that wants a shorter country list.
internal.who_should_get_it: International orgs that do not want the full ISO list on forms.
internal.gotchas: Need Organization Settings update permission. Phone default is a starting country, not a locked country.

entries.title: Email Send Date merge tags, and days-until on formula fields
entries.summary: Campaigns can insert **Email Send Date** and **+ 7 / 14 / 30 Days**, resolved when the email actually goes out — a recurring campaign uses that run's day. Formula fields can use `days_until` and `add_days` on a date field and still store a number.

where.path: Send → campaign → Basic info → Merge tags; Settings → Fields → Formula

entries.use_case: A weekly reminder can say reply by the send date plus seven days without rewriting the draft each week, and a Days until visa expiry column stays a number.

cs_action.note: Send-date tags resolve at send, not preview-as-draft-day. Formula date helpers are UTC whole days.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Recurring campaigns with a reply-by line; visa or membership countdown columns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone writing date-relative email copy or countdown fields.
internal.gotchas: add_days still returns a number (days from today to date+N), not a new date string.

entries.title: Add a contact to a session from their Program tab
entries.summary: On a contact, the **Program** tab has **Add to session**. Pick the session and role without opening the session first. Adding them to the event also queues portal membership so Assigned Portal and tasks catch up without re-saving portal filters.

where.path: CRM → contact → Program → Add to session

entries.use_case: A CSM already looking at a speaker can put them on the keynote from the contact, instead of hunting the session Participants tab.

cs_action.note: Hidden when the contact is on no event. Portal sync is the Event_Module_Records hook (SB-9633).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Assigned Portal stayed empty after adding a contact to the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone building a program from the contact side.
internal.gotchas: The contact must already be on the event. Role list is the event's participant roles.
